findings.title: Raw-HTML hardening the PR claims is not implemented
findings.body: The PR's security model says two things the code does not do: - Raw HTML `src` is rewritten to `#` when the setting is OFF. This whole block runs only `if (allowLocalImages)`. - `srcset` is removed in both states. No code touches `srcset`. As a result, `` or a `data:` `src` still renders, and `srcset` candidates bypass the `src` validation. Fix: implement the described sanitisation (run the `src` rewrite in both states and strip `srcset`), or correct the security claims.

findings.body: The regex `\ssrc\s*=\s*"([^"]+)"` only matches double-quoted values. These forms pass through untouched: - `` - `` - `` When local images are ON, the old `` whose `src` was not rewritten.

findings.title: No reparse-point check before serving files despite PR's stated protection
findings.body:
The PR claims junctions and symlinks below the allowed path are rejected by checking `FileAttributes.ReparsePoint` on each path component. Neither `TryResolveVirtualUrl` nor this handler does that: they check containment lexically and then call `File.ReadAllBytes`.

Trigger: a folder containing a symlink or junction (e.g. a cloned repo with symlinks, or an extracted archive). It can make the preview read and display files outside the document folder or share.

Fix: walk the resolved path's components and refuse any with `ReparsePoint`, or resolve the final target and re-check containment. Also consider restricting serving to image extensions, since any file type is currently served.

findings.title: Settings read failures other than a missing file break the whole preview
findings.body:
`GetLocalImagesEnabled` catches only `FileNotFoundException`. It is called inside `DoPreview`'s try block, before the markdown is rendered.

Trigger: the settings file is being written by the Settings app (an `IOException` sharing violation), its directory is missing, or the JSON is corrupt. The exception escapes, and the preview shows the error state instead of the markdown with images blocked.

Fix: catch broadly (e.g. `Exception`) and return `false`, or use a get-or-default settings helper.

held.title: UNC share-root detection widens the allowed base for `\\?\` and `\\.\` paths
held.body:
Any directory starting with `\\` is treated as a UNC share, and the base becomes the first two segments.

Trigger: Explorer hands over an extended-length path. Then:
- `\\?\C:\docs` gives a base of `\\?\C:`, so the entire drive becomes servable.
- `\\?\UNC\server\share\...` gives a base of `\\?\UNC`, which covers every server.

I could not confirm whether the preview handler ever receives such paths.

Fix: normalise `\\?\` and `\\.\` prefixes first (map `\\?\UNC\` to `\\`, strip `\\?\` for drive paths) before computing the share root. Alternatively, fall back to the markdown directory for anything that is not a plain `\\server\share`.
